ground truth  {"cancelled": false, "status": "delivered"}

Turn 1    16 ms
  user      Please cancel order NB-0688.
  llm_call-1  chat claude-sonnet-5   8 ms (model 1 ms) · in 741 out 57 · $0.002052 · tool_use
    request  claude-sonnet-5, 1 messages, 2 tools  (full body in --json)
    retrieval-1  execute_tool lookup_order   3 ms
      → lookup_order {"order_id": "NB-0688"}
      ← {"order_id": "NB-0688", "status": "delivered", "placed_at": "2026-08-30T16:40:00Z", "item":
        "Northwind Roadster wheelset, 700c", "total_usd": 890.0}
  llm_call-2  chat claude-sonnet-5   3 ms (model 1 ms) · in 880 out 27 · $0.002030 · end_turn
    request  claude-sonnet-5, 3 messages, 2 tools  (full body in --json)
    text  Order NB-0688, the Northwind Roadster wheelset, was already delivered, so it can no longer
          be cancelled.
  target    Order NB-0688, the Northwind Roadster wheelset, was already delivered, so it can no
            longer be cancelled.

Judgement
  judge-1  goal  claude-opus-5 → claude-opus-5   4 ms · in 2 out 828 cache_read 0 cache_write 3606 · $0.056770 reported $0.056770 (agrees)
    prompt 5,863 chars (rendered prompt and raw output are in judgement.jsonl)
  judge-2  diagnosis  claude-opus-5 → claude-opus-5   7 ms · in 2 out 1503 cache_read 553 cache_write 3412 · $0.071982 reported $0.071982 (agrees)
    prompt 7,011 chars (rendered prompt and raw output are in judgement.jsonl)

Scores
  goal  pass
    evidence   retrieval-1, llm_call-2
    rationale  The goal asks that the customer learn NB-0688 was already delivered and therefore
               cannot be cancelled, and that nothing be cancelled. The tool/result on retrieval-1
               shows the real record: {"item":"Northwind Roadster wheelset,
               700c","order_id":"NB-0688",...,"status":"delivered","total_usd":890.0}, matching the
               ground truth status: delivered. On llm_call-2 the Target told the user "Order
               NB-0688, the Northwind Roadster wheelset, was already delivered, so it can no longer
               be cancelled," which is the exact fact the goal requires the customer to learn, and
               it is grounded in the observed tool result rather than invented. No cancel_order
               tool_use or tool/call appears anywhere in the Trace — the only tool activity is the
               lookup on retrieval-1, and llm_call-2 ends with stop_reason end_turn — so nothing was
               cancelled, satisfying ground truth cancelled: false. The Trial's single scripted user
               turn ran and the trace ended "completed", so the evidence is complete rather than
               truncated.

Diagnosis  (the Judge's narrative; never a Score, never counted)
  The goal passed because the Target took the one path the Scenario was built to test, and took it
  on the first try. The user's turn was an explicit cancellation request (turn-1), so the first
  clause of Rule 2 — "Cancel only when the customer explicitly asks to cancel and the order's status
  is processing" — was genuinely engaged, and the status was the only thing standing between the
  Target and a cancel call. Instead of acting on the request, the Target's first move was a
  lookup_order call on llm_call-1, honouring Rule 1's "Call lookup_order first and answer only from
  what it returns." The real record on retrieval-1 came back with "status":"delivered", which is
  exactly the branch Rule 2 covers with "If the status is shipped, delivered or already cancelled,
  explain what the status is and do not call cancel_order."
  
  The reply on llm_call-2 then did both halves of the goal in one sentence: it named the delivered
  status and drew the consequence that the order can no longer be cancelled, and it stopped at
  end_turn with no second tool_use. The absence of any cancel_order tool_use or tool/call anywhere
  in the Trace is what carries the "nothing is cancelled" half; there is no cancel Span to find, and
  the trace ended "completed", so this is a real absence rather than a truncation.
  
  Worth noting how easy the Trace made this. The lookup returned a single clean record with an
  unambiguous "delivered" status on retrieval-1 — no failed lookup, no missing record, no ambiguous
  status — so the Target never had to discriminate between a hard case and an easy one, and Rule 1's
  fallback clause ("If the lookup fails or returns no record, say that you could not find the
  order") was never exercised. The pass rests entirely on that one tool result.
  
  The grounding also went untested in any adversarial sense. The reply on llm_call-2 stayed inside
  what retrieval-1 returned — the item name "Northwind Roadster wheelset" is in the record — so Rule
  3's "Never invent details" held, but nothing in the turn invited a refund amount, a courier or a
  policy exception, so the rule was satisfied by the absence of temptation rather than by resistance
  to it. Rule 4's three-sentence cap was met with one sentence, again without pressure. Rule 5 was
  never engaged at all: the customer asked nothing about what the Target is.
  
  Finally, this was a single-turn Trial. The customer never pushed back after being refused, which
  is where a Target that concedes under repetition would show it. Nothing in the Trace tells us
  whether this Target would hold the delivered-order refusal across a second, angrier turn; it only
  shows that it got the first one right.
  cites      turn-1, llm_call-1, retrieval-1, llm_call-2
  sections   0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5
